content: Tetracycline is an antibiotic used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections, including acne. It is not effective against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. This medication works by inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis through binding to the 30S and possibly the 50S ribosomal subunits. When taking tetracycline, it is important to follow specific instructions to ensure its effectiveness and minimize side effects. Take the medication on an empty stomach, at least one hour before or two hours after meals, as directed by your doctor. If stomach upset occurs, consult your doctor about taking it with food. Each dose should be taken with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) to reduce the risk of esophageal irritation or ulceration. Avoid lying down for at least 10 minutes after taking the medication. Tetracycline should not be taken with products containing aluminum, calcium, iron, magnesium, zinc, or bismuth subsalicylate, as these can impair its absorption. Examples include antacids, quinapril, sucralfate, vitamins/minerals, dairy products (e.g., milk, yogurt), and calcium-enriched juice. Take tetracycline 2 to 3 hours before or after consuming these products. The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For optimal results, take the medication at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects of tetracycline include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, loss of appetite, mouth sores, black hairy tongue, sore throat, dizziness, headache, and rectal discomfort. Rarely, it may cause increased pressure around the brain (intracranial hypertension), which is more likely in overweight women of childbearing age or those with a history of this condition. If intracranial hypertension develops, it usually resolves after stopping the medication, but there is a risk of permanent vision loss or blindness. Tetracycline may also rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to Clostridium difficile bacteria, which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Prolonged or repeated use may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection (oral or vaginal fungal infection). Serious allergic reactions to tetracycline are rare but possible. This medication can make you more sensitive to sunlight, so limit sun exposure, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Tetracycline should not be used in children under 8 years of age, as it may cause permanent tooth discoloration and other issues. Tooth discoloration has also been reported in older children and young adults. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor. Tetracycline should not be used during pregnancy, as it may harm an unborn baby. It also passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how tetracycline works or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Tetracycline may interfere with certain lab tests, potentially causing false results. Store tetracycline at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or no longer needed medication, as taking outdated tetracycline can result in serious illness. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
